title: Commitment-backed capacity slices and residency-safe evacuation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers running Redwood Dedicated need bounded, contract-backed throughput guarantees (capacity slices) inside regional fleets while preserving data residency constraints during zone/region evacuations. Current autoscaling and failover mechanisms either (a) overprovision to meet top-line SLA at high cost or (b) fail open and route requests to a non-resident region, which violates compliance for some customers.

This ticket introduces a design and implementation for "commitment-backed capacity slices": customer-scoped reservations expressed as throughput slices (tokens/sec or concurrent streams) with an evacuation-safe failover plan. Key goals: (1) honor committed throughput while minimizing overprovisioning, (2) ensure any failover obeys data residency constraints and explicit customer policies, and (3) let autoscaler operate within bounded headroom to absorb short spikes without violating residency or SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: API: Customers can create or modify a commitment-backed slice on a Dedicated pool with: slice_id, committed_tokens_per_minute, region_constraints (allowlist/denylist), failover_mode (none, region-local, degrade-within-region), and min_headroom_pct.
Runtime: The scheduler allocates capacity slices to machines in the regional multi-zone pool and tracks per-slice committed usage with 1-minute resolution accounting.

Autoscaler: Autoscaler respects per-slice min_headroom_pct and will only scale pool capacity within pre-authorized zones. It must not perform cross-region routing that violates region_constraints for active slices.

Failover: When a zone drain or capacity loss occurs, the system applies slice.failover_mode to decide routing; for 'degrade-within-region', requests are gracefully shed by priority and soft-evicted clients receive structured error with suggested retry windows and allowed regions.
SLOs: For committed slices, the platform meets 95th percentile token throughput >= committed_tokens_per_minute - 10% over any 10-minute window under normal region conditions (no full-region outage).
Observability: New dashboards exist showing per-slice commit vs observed throughput, per-slice residency compliance events, and a runbook link for forced evacuations.
Migration: Existing Dedicated customers can opt into converting reserved pools into commitment-backed slices without downtime via a guided migration flow in Console.
technical_notes:
Design overview: 1) Slice abstraction: lightweight tenant object with commit metadata stored in config-store and cached at scheduler. 2) Bounded headroom: slices include min_headroom_pct (default 10%) that the autoscaler can use to absorb burst; headroom is carved from uncommitted pool capacity and cannot be moved cross-region unless policy permits. 3) Placement: allocation algorithm attempts zone-local placement first, then region-local if needed, avoiding cross-region assignment unless allowed by region_constraints. 4) Failover modes: none (no cross-zone/region routing; requests fail), region-local (route within same AWS region across surviving AZs), degrade-within-region (best-effort degrade with structured fallback). 5) Accounting and throttling: token-leaky-bucket per-slice at proxy entrypoint; a global per-pool admission controller enforces safety caps to prevent domino failures.

Implementation notes: - Extend pool config schema with 'slices' map; - Scheduler to run allocation delta every 30s and emit rebalancing plans; - Autoscaler hooks: expose allocate_headroom(slice_id, requested_extra) and drain_for_evacuate(slice_id, zone); - Add residency policy check in router and admission controller that returns residency_violation events and blocks route if policy prohibits.

Security: Committed slice metadata may include residency constraints that are security-sensitive. All slice config changes must go through audit-logged endpoints and require org-admin role. KMS-protect slice metadata in the config-store replication path.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement slice objects and local accounting; API gated behind feature-flag 'commitment-slices', enable for internal test org and 2 pilot customers. Phase 2: scheduler placement + autoscaler integration; run in passive mode (monitor-only) for 2 weeks. Phase 3: enforcement and Console controls + customer migration UI. Phase 4: wider rollout with tuned autoscaler defaults and SLA articulation. Rollback path: disable enforcement flag and revert routing changes; queued requests preserved for 60s then fail-safe routed only if customer allows cross-region.
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocation math, e2e integration tests simulating zone-loss and verifying failover modes, chaos test in staging (kill 1 AZ, then 2 AZs) to validate 'degrade-within-region' behavior, perf test to ensure 1-minute accounting scales to 5k slices per region with <5% CPU overhead. Run regression suite against Console migration flow. Include a security integration test to verify audit logs for slice config changes are emitted.
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Initial spike findings: storing slice state in the existing config-store adds ~6ms to scheduler read path; recommend caching with TTL 15s.

2026-02-28 Priya Singh (SRE): Chaos tests show that without a soft-eviction algorithm, heavy slices can cause noisy-neighbor effect during AZ drain; we should implement fairness arbitration based on slice priority and age.
2026-03-03 Omar Patel: Prototype of token-leaky-bucket implemented; needs optimization to reduce lock contention at 5k slices. Planned to switch to sharded counters.
2026-03-08 Legal (Elena Ruiz): Residency constraints must be surfaced to billing and contracts; please add a field in slice metadata to mark 'sovereign' customers for extra audit retention.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Security review scheduled; assigned to Security team for KMS integration and audit schema review.
